clue.text: Immediately taking on economy, without any fancy trimmings

indicators.note: taking on means one piece adds the next after it

parts.note: to go straight away is to go immediately
an economy is a cut in spending

explanation.surface: Someone making savings at once, refusing any frills.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain, simple cut, as of hair or cloth, has no fancy shaping or decoration.

clue.text: Host for www.churchofengland.org?

parts.note: a website is hosted by an internet company, but a church literally lays on worship services for its people

explanation.surface: Who hosts the Church of England's website?
explanation.walkthrough: The web address makes you think of an internet hosting firm; the second reading is the Church itself, which provides services of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet company that hosts sites is the usual sense; a church laying on worship gives the pun.

clue.text: A sailor getting upset about one stock controller

indicators.note: about means the reversed letters go round the numeral
in a down clue upset means the letter and the sailor's word are turned upside down, read from bottom up

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sailor is distressed by a lone cattle hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns A TAR into RATA, and 'about' wraps that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A riata is a lariat or lasso, used by cowboys to control livestock.

clue.text: Popular composer presented in edition? There's a surprise

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: presented in means the composer's name is placed within the abbreviation

parts.note: Verdi is the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A famous composer appears in a new printing, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of astonishment; both phrases express mild amazement at news.

clue.text: Was very much against a horrible death

indicators.note: horrible suggests something mangled, so the letters of the word death are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone strongly opposed a gruesome end.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to be very much against it; a past-tense verb matching 'Was'.

clue.text: Cooked each short Passover meal

indicators.note: cooked suggests the words each and short are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Each item was prepared for a brief festive dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like it shortens a word, but it is part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Charoseth is a sweet fruit-and-nut paste eaten at the Jewish Seder, the Passover feast.

clue.text: The trendy dealer works with great care

indicators.note: works means the letters of the three words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A fashionable trader goes about business very carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with kindly, gentle concern is acting with great care and compassion.

clue.text: Style regarding publication clear: it's always attractive

parts.note: a perm is a hairstyle
anent is an old word meaning regarding or concerning
mag is short for magazine, a publication
to net is to clear as profit

explanation.surface: A hairdo featured in a clear magazine story is always appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attractive' is meant magnetically, not as good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet that keeps its magnetism indefinitely always pulls iron towards it.

clue.text: Sign of gratitude after aircraft takes one into curious view of the sky

indicators.note: after means the thanks word follows the aircraft word

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft
ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: into means the numeral goes inside the word for curious

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A passenger thanks the crew as a plane gives a strange look at the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: A planetarium projects a view of the night sky onto a domed ceiling.

clue.text: Doctor satisfied in there, getting right item used in diagnosis

indicators.note: in means the doctor and satisfied words go inside the word there

parts.note: taken as written
MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to meet a need is to satisfy it, so met

explanation.surface: A doctor is content in the surgery, picking up the right tool for a diagnosis.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor takes a temperature reading with this instrument to help diagnose fever.

clue.text: Trouble? It's brought in a crowd

indicators.note: brought in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a gate is the crowd attending a sports match
the clue reads 'it is', so the word it

explanation.surface: Is there trouble when a crowd is let in?
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to disturb or worry them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Stop limiting church in extra large religious region

indicators.note: limiting means the stop word encloses the rest

parts.note: to die is to stop, as an engine dies

indicators.note: in means the church letters go within the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS means outsize, extra large
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Stop restricting the church to a very large religious district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a command but is a synonym; 'in' and 'limiting' nest the pieces to give OCES within DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocese is the district under a bishop's authority.

clue.text: Still activity at sea when the nights are drawing in

definitions.text: when the nights are drawing in

parts.note: even can mean still, as in 'even better'
tides are the ebb and flow of the sea

explanation.surface: Calm movements on the water as autumn evenings close in.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the time when night draws on.

clue.text: Strangled the Duke, suppressing corruption before heartless trial

indicators.note: suppressing means the outer words hold the rest down inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: before means the decay word comes ahead of the trimmed trial

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption

indicators.note: heartless means trial loses its middle, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: A nobleman was strangled while covering up a corrupt, cruel trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' keeps only the outside letters of trial; 'suppressing' sets the corruption and those letters inside the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle is to choke someone by the throat; past tense matches.

clue.text: Exotic fish goes and swims around right area

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the others
swims suggests the letters of goes and swirl into a new order

explanation.surface: An unusual fish heads off and swims about in a certain patch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swims' makes SEADGON, and 'around' sets RA in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A seadragon is a leafy relative of the seahorse found off Australia.

clue.text: Sorcerer retreated, having kidnapped husband in Surrey town

indicators.note: having kidnapped means the reversed word holds the letter inside
retreated means the sorcerer word goes backwards

parts.note: a mage is a magician or sorcerer

explanation.surface: A wizard fled after abducting a man in a southern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreated' turns MAGE into EGAM. Egham is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Egham is a town in the English county of Surrey, near Windsor.

clue.text: Laundry accessory increasingly just not opening

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: fairer means more just

explanation.surface: A washing gadget that is getting fairer but won't open.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an airer is a rack on which washed clothes are hung to dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse or rack for drying washing is a household laundry item.

clue.text: Yielded, returning personnel before important meeting for major part of body

indicators.note: before means personnel comes ahead of the meeting
returning means the word for yielded is read backwards

parts.note: an investment that paid has yielded a return
HR is human resources, the personnel department
an AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: Staff gave in, going back before the big annual meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The diaphragm is the large muscle separating the chest from the abdomen.

clue.text: Requested change to divine right, ultimately

indicators.note: change to means the letters are rearranged
ultimately means the last letter of the word right

explanation.surface: A petition to alter the divine right of kings.
explanation.definitionFit: To be invited is to be asked, so requested to come.

clue.text: Imagine 500 sheets of paper (500)

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Picture a stack of 500 sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream up something is to imagine it.

clue.text: Scoundrel's attorney receiving a rap

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel; the 's joins the next piece

indicators.note: receiving means the abbreviation takes the letter inside

parts.note: att. is the abbreviation for attorney

explanation.surface: A villain's lawyer gets a reprimand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rap' looks like a legal reprimand in the surface, but it is a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat-a-tat is the sound of repeated knocking, a rap at the door.

clue.text: Revolutionary skill taking care of excellent item of jewellery

indicators.note: revolutionary means the built letters turn right round
taking care of means the skill word holds the other inside it

parts.note: art is skill
A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A radical craft creates a fine piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking care of' gives AAIRT, which 'Revolutionary' turns round; A1 for excellent is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headband or crown worn on formal occasions.

clue.text: Conservative unfortunately meddled with learning

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory has sadly interfered with education.
explanation.walkthrough: Middle England is the conservative, middle-class English heartland, often named in British political talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Middle England is typified as traditional and politically right-leaning.

clue.text: Regret introducing stupid new article in trial — not fully thought through

indicators.note: introducing means the regret word takes the stupid word inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret
dim means stupid

indicators.note: in means the article goes inside the trial word

parts.note: a try is an attempt or trial
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone regrets bringing a foolish new clause into a court case — half-baked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rudimentary is basic and undeveloped, only at an early stage.
